codeReview.budgetStructure: Budget<'work, 'owner> with one added field shared: Option<&'work mut opensip_platform::WorkScope<'owner>>

codeReview.varianceAnalysis: &'work mut WorkScope<'owner> is covariant in 'work and invariant in 'owner, because WorkScope holds &'owner mut WorkLedger. A Budget<'static,'static> therefore cannot stand in for a borrowed Budget<'w,'o>.

codeReview.dropGuardIsPanicSafe: scope and the platform LedgerScope::drop only flip a bool, so nothing can unwind out of this Drop during an unwind
codeReview.dropGuardIsIdempotent: calling it on an already-failed ledger returns Closed immediately

limits: Acceptance covers ten files and retained accounting ONLY. This is explicitly not complete native precharge.
Existing capture callbacks may allocate and read before retention, and native directory open or observation may precede the directory object charge.
Names, ACLs, parsing, rechecks, temporary buffers and post-effect reservations remain unaccounted and need later native work.
HostCapture is not qualified by this change. No host attempt, native creator, public ingress, permit, P0, custody or current authority is claimed, and no M2 or M2-M6 completion.
The private 422 reader and 413 ACL prototypes are not included and are not approved.
Constructors remain accounting, not authority; the obligation to keep the ledger owner private still sits with the future host.
macOS development evidence only; no Linux, crash, power-loss or release qualification.
Root substantive assent and guarded private/live verification remain required before selection.
observations: work() returns Error::Profile when there is no shared scope, overloading a variant that otherwise means invalid budget profile parameters. Reusing existing variants was a constraint, so this is a reasonable trade, but a caller cannot distinguish the two conditions; a doc line would help, and a dedicated variant would be better whenever the error enum next opens.

borrowed() hardcodes the global ceilings and cannot fail, so it offers no way to tighten local caps the way new() does; per-operation tightening must come from the platform ledger's with_limits. Coherent, but the asymmetry with new() deserves a doc note.

The Drop guard closes the shared scope with a synthetic WorkFailure::Operation(()). Nothing is lost today because the platform ledger records only the latch, but a post-mortem sees Closed with no indication of which security operation closed it.

One logical charge can traverse several guards (scope -> guard -> account -> platform charge -> platform scope). Harmless, but worth knowing when reading a trace: a caught failure at any depth latches both ledgers.

The accounting gap deserves restating rather than burying: retention is charged, physical capture is not. Any later adapter that reads or allocates before retention is spending unaccounted work, and this acceptance does not cover it.
